name: New retail / secondary asking market: RTX 4090 and RTX 3090 24GB (bare card bands)
price_basis: SECONDARY-MARKET ASKING prices, bare consumer 24GB GeForce cards, USD, observed 2026-10-03. NOT new-retail and NOT sold prices - these are live Buy-It-Now asks on a resale marketplace. Excludes tax/shipping.
notes: OBSERVATION DATE 2026-10-03. Source sup-price-picclick-ebay-asking. TWO BANDS, both 2026-10-03, bare cards only: RTX 4090 24GB n=35 after title filtering, quartiles $2,693 / $3,299 / $3,600, full observed range $1,800-$5,000; RTX 3090 24GB n=72, quartiles $1,300 / $1,514 / $1,600, full observed range $899-$2,500. price_usd is the 4090 median. CONDITION IS UNKNOWABLE HERE - the central caveat. PicClick's Condition parameter returns byte-identical pages (verified 2026-10-03), so these listings mix new-in-box, open-box-return and genuinely used cards with no way to tell them apart from the page. Within the 3090 band the ambiguity is visible in the titles themselves ('New Sealed' at $2,000 and 'Excellent Condition' at $1,529 in the same distribution), which is direct evidence that condition and price are entangled. Do not read the top of this band as a new-retail price. EXCLUDED: complete systems and laptops (the RTX 4090 set included 5 Alienware/Lenovo laptops priced $1,800-$2,580, which would drag the band down ~20% if included), the $4,950-$5,555 modded-48GB RTX 4090s, FOR-PARTS units, and one QUADRO RTX 6000 mislabelled in a 3090 query.
